elements.text:
A /bsolar eclipse/z happens when the moon passes directly between the world and the sun. The moon is far smaller, but it is also far nearer, so from the ground the two look almost exactly the same size, and for a short while the moon covers the sun completely.

  That is why you never see the moon during one. It is there, but it is the dark side facing you, with all the sunlight falling on the far side. The stars stay hidden too: the sky is dim, but not truly night, so they are never drawn out.

  Expect one roughly every /b20 to 30 days/z. They only ever begin while the sun is already up.

  It arrives in /bfive stages/z, about fifteen seconds apart, each darker than the last: Newborn, Rising, Half Veil, Umbral, and finally /bTotal Eclipse/z. Totality holds for /beight minutes/z, then the same five stages run backwards until the sun is whole again.

  While it lasts the day does not advance. The sun stays where it was caught and the day count stands still, so no eclipse will ever cost you a day.

  Hostile creatures read the dark as their own. They come out in /btwice/z their usual numbers and hit /bdouble/z as hard.

  For an /b/umbramancyumbramancer/z there is no better hour. Every shadow working is /btwice as strong/z and lasts /btwice as long/z. Older astral writers held that shadow is not simply absent light but a substance in its own right, thinner than air and normally spread too wide to grasp. An eclipse, they wrote, is the one moment it gathers.

  This mechanic's visuals will not work well with shaders.
